kite2.overall: CONDITIONAL / NOT CREDIBLE AS SPECIFIED. This is the most original concept and the one most worth refining. The modelling is careful and fully reproducible, and the controls idea (glide for elevation, roll for azimuth, winch-flown retrieve) is sound. But the headline result depends on an untested coefficient corner (CR 0.2 at L/D ~0.5–0.7). If a 0.35 m² soft canopy cannot fly there, the pull and footage claims fail (gust force 54–89 N, avail 50–84 %). The mass is under-budgeted (realistic 75–113 g, so the fast-mode KE fails at ≥85 g). Lift auto-launch, line-behind-rider hazard and resort kiting bans are major but fixable or scope-limiting. Nothing is fatal yet in physics, but finding K2-01 becomes fatal if a tow test shows CR ≥0.5 at L/D ≤0.8.
kite2.envelope: Permitted terrain only (no resort kiting ban). Open, low-traffic groomed run with nobody within ~5 m behind, no trees within ~15 m, no lifts overhead. Continuous carving at 8–16 m/s (fast-mode KE marginal at realistic mass). Ambient wind ≤6 m/s with no tailwind component above ~0.3 × rider speed in short turns. Moguls/steep slopes accept a ~50° top-down view. Each stop costs ~2.5 s of footage on restart. Expect a manual push-in at 10–25 % of stops. Disarm before every lift.
kite2.summary: Reproducible, dt-converged, honest about most limits. The decisive unknown is whether a small soft canopy can be simultaneously depowered (CR 0.2) and parachutal (L/D 0.5) while staying inflated and steerable. Literature suggests low L/D occurs only at high AoA with CR ~0.8–1.1. The next step is a tow-test polar, not more simulation.

towglider.overall: CONDITIONAL. No fatal physics: following a skier by gravity glide, with the leash topping up the drag shortfall, is sound at the operating point, and the follow footage is robust. It fails the harmonised targets as specified on three counts: endurance in the cold unless the holster is heated, standstill and ops in real runs with rest stops or windy unplanned stops, and a 95 g mass that relies on a gimbal that does not exist at 12 g. Regulatory exposure is high: US VLOS, resort bans, and EU registration.
towglider.envelope: Open, uncrowded 10–18° pistes; rider 8–15 m/s at a realistic 115–125 g (6–16 m/s only if 95 g is reached); carving or short turns; mean wind ≤5–6 m/s for unplanned stops (≤9 m/s only when docking while moving); ≤1 rest stop per run; EU/UK A1 with operator registration and written resort permission; holster heated for charging.
towglider.summary: Original and physically sensible: the slope pays for flight and a 0.12–1 N leash replaces the battery-heavy hover. The model is careful and mostly honest (fast and I-05 failures reported, L/D −30 % run). The main gaps are a seed-favourable stop_wind result (the cutter fires in half of 9 m/s seeds), the missing per-run stop accounting, cold charging, gimbal mass, and an unverified wake dock.

leapfrog.overall: NOT FATAL – CONDITIONAL / FRAGILE PASS. Physically sound core (gravity pays a ≤15 m/s lead flight; it is the only concept with a head-on view and keeps VLOS in front of the user). By the shared definitions it fails ops (3 vs ≤2). Its footage and KE passes rest on three optimistic assumptions: a 125 g mass (audit ≈160–175 g), full-resolution 50 MP video readout, and a perfectly stabilised 10 g turret. Load-bearing manoeuvres (perching flare, snow take-off, pole snatch) and resort permission/bystander exposure are unverified. Fixable engineering, not a physics kill; resort acceptance may be the real kill.
leapfrog.envelope: Groomed firm (not icy, not soft) piste ≥35 m wide, slope 6–25° (motor-assisted below ~10°), low traffic, mean wind ≤4–6 m/s (crosswind gusts unreliable), rider downhill progress ≈8–11.5 m/s (vTarget ≤13 m/s at a realistic 160–175 g; ≤14 m/s only at the claimed 125 g), only where the resort permits UAS; fallback lead-only mode for faster/slower riders not demonstrated.
leapfrog.summary: Original and the most interesting viewpoint of round 2; the metrics claims are reproducible but optimistic in mass, sensor readout and frame-relative jitter, and ops is mis-counted. Recommend: honest BOM, effective-resolution and frame-normalised jitter re-runs, ops=3 or a snatch-to-stow redesign, then a physical perching/take-off test series as the gate.

descentglider.overall: NOT YET CREDIBLE as specified; physically sound idea with an honest aero model, but its pass list rests on an unjustified 380 Wh/kg micro pack and a 30 s stop-free nominal. Fixable-major, not fatal: no single law of physics is violated, but the coupled mass-KE-cap-catch-up loop leaves very little margin.
descentglider.envelope: Within the model: groomed slope of about 12-22°, rider steady at 8-13 m/s with no more than about 1 stop per 2-3 min, wind ≤5 m/s with tailwind component <5 m/s (tip-over on perch above about 5-6 m/s off-span), no crowding, and a resort that allows drones. Expect about 60-70 % usable footage per full run (launch and catch-up losses) and about 35-45 min per charge at a realistic 150-165 g. Out of envelope: riders above 13-14 m/s, short turns and moguls (<80 %), tailwind ≥5 m/s, lift-queue landings, US VLOS rules and Vail-type bans.
descentglider.summary: Gravity-paid gliding follow is credible (L/D 7.9 honest, pFollow 3.5-4.2 W in carving), and the perch-at-stops idea is original. The pass list is inflated by the 22 g/8.5 Wh battery (380 Wh/kg), an 18 g/1.6 W 4K pan-tilt camera and a stop-free 30 s nominal. At a realistic mass the KE cap (≤14.9 J gives ~12.9 m/s) stops it catching a 12 m/s rider after a launch or perch (cycle avail 5 %). setupTime p90 is 34 s or more when wind directions are randomised.

crossConcept.note: Glider aero is mutually consistent in form (parabolic low-Re polar, CLmax 1.0, e 0.75–0.8) and none uses L/D better than its CD0/AR justify; all three ran a −30 % L/D sensitivity. Re is 30–90 k, partly below the brief band of 50–150 k; at Re ≈30 k CLmax ≈0.85 is more defensible than 1.0 (stall +0.4–0.5 m/s). The real non-comparabilities are battery specific energy (descent 380 vs 150–185 Wh/kg), cold charging from worn banks (kite, tow, leap), camera power (1.6–2.5 W), reserve (10 vs 15 %), the absence of stops in every nominal, and mass budgets that are uniformly 20–40 % light. kite2 uses effective coefficients with no Re dependence and is not comparable to the glider polars; its key unknown (CR 0.2 at L/D ≈0.5–0.7) is a single tow test.
